paper_title: On the Edge Density of Bipartite 3-Planar and Bipartite Gap-Planar Graphs
statement: We have established tight upper bounds on the number of edges of bipartite gap-planar and bipartite 3-planar graphs. The following questions follow naturally: What is the density of bipartite k-planar graphs, in particular for k = 4? One could most likely apply the discharging method in a similar way for any fixed k – the issue that arises for larger k is just the sheer number of cases one has to consider. Hence, we ask as an open problem if one can (partially) automate such a charging proof in a similar way to [4]. This is of course also an interesting question in the normal (non-bipartite) setting. A graph is quasi-planar if there is a drawing in which no three edges mutually cross. What is the edge density of bipartite quasi-planar graphs?
